examples.en: The ramen water boiled over and made the stove dirty.
The milk will boil over, so turn the heat down.
I didn't notice until the soup was boiling over.

examples.ko: 냄비 뚜껑을 살짝 열어 두면 덜 끓어넘쳐요.
examples.en: If you leave the pot lid slightly open, it boils over less.
The porridge boiled over and spilled on the floor.
Even when my anger felt ready to boil over, I held it in.

explain: 요리할 때 국이나 우유, 라면 물이 끓으면서 냄비 밖으로 넘치는 상황에 많이 써요. '끓어오르다'는 끓으면서 위로 올라오는 것까지만 말하고, 끓어넘치다는 밖으로 넘치는 것을 말해요. 감정이 매우 커진 모습에 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: If you turn the heat up high, the soup boils over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 또는 자주 일어나는 일을 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite present form for what happens now or often.

phrases.example: 끓어넘치지 않게 냄비 뚜껑을 조금 열어 두세요.
phrases.en: Leave the pot lid slightly open so it doesn't boil over.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않게'를 붙여 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-지 않게' to say how to prevent it.

phrases.example: 잠깐 전화를 받는 사이에 우유가 끓어넘쳤어요.
phrases.en: The milk boiled over while I answered a call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우유처럼 거품이 많은 음식에서 자주 일어나는 상황이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common accident with foamy liquids like milk.

explain_en: Liquid boiling and spilling out of a pot (라면 물이 끓어넘치다) It is mostly used in cooking, when soup, milk, or ramen water boils and spills out of the pot. '끓어오르다' means the liquid only rises up while boiling, while '끓어넘치다' means it spills out. It can also be used figuratively for strong emotions.

t90.ax: The milk will boil over, so turn the heat down.

examples.en: The lamb has a gamey smell.
To get rid of the gamey smell, add ginger.
This meat is tender with no gamey smell.

examples.ko: 노린내에 민감한 사람은 이 요리를 싫어해요.
examples.en: People who are sensitive to gamey smells dislike this dish.

examples.ko: 염소 고기는 노린내 때문에 호불호가 갈려요.
examples.en: Goat meat divides people because of its gamey smell.

examples.ko: 노린내도 거의 안 나서 먹을 만했어요.
examples.en: It hardly had any gamey smell, so it was good enough to eat.

explain: 양고기나 염소 고기처럼 짐승 고기에서 나는 특유의 냄새예요. 생선이나 날것에서 나는 냄새는 '비린내'라고 해서 구분해요. 요리할 때 '노린내를 잡다'처럼 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I soak the meat in milk to get rid of its gamey smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 냄새를 없앤다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for removing smell when cooking.

phrases.example: 이 고기는 노린내가 심해서 먹기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: This meat has a strong gamey smell, so it's hard to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새가 강해서 불편할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the smell is strong and unpleasant.

phrases.en: I don't like meat that smells gamey.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나는'으로 명사를 꾸며 냄새가 나는 음식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 나는 to modify a noun, describing food with that smell.

explain_en: It is the particular smell of animal meat such as lamb or goat. The smell of fish or raw food is called '비린내', so the two are kept apart. In cooking people say things like '노린내를 잡다' (to get rid of the gamey smell).

en: to be scorched; to burn; to burn to the bottom of a pot or pan

examples.en: The rice stuck and burned onto the bottom of the pot.

examples.ko: 불을 세게 켜면 고기가 팬에 눌어붙어요.
examples.en: If you turn up the heat, the meat sticks and burns on the pan.

examples.ko: 눌어붙은 찌꺼기를 닦는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to scrub off the burnt-on residue.

examples.ko: 기름을 안 두르면 계란이 눌어붙을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't add oil, the egg can stick and burn.

examples.ko: 국이 눌어붙지 않게 가끔 저어 주세요.
examples.en: Please stir the soup now and then so it doesn't stick and burn.

examples.ko: 냄비에 우유가 눌어붙어서 탄 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: Milk has burned onto the pot, so it smells burnt.

explain: 열 때문에 음식이 그릇에 붙으면서 조금 타는 것을 말해요. '타다'는 많이 까맣게 태우는 느낌이고, '눌어붙다'는 바닥에 딱 붙은 상태에 초점이 있어요. '눌어붙은 밥', '눌은밥'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I scraped the rice stuck to the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눌어붙다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾸면 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 눌어붙다 used before a noun.
phrases.en_equiv: scorched rice stuck to the pot

phrases.en: Food doesn't stick to this pan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 도구를 소개할 때 자주 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form often used when describing cookware.
phrases.en_equiv: does not stick or burn on

phrases.en: I poured water on the scorched rice and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥에 눌어붙은 밥, 또는 그것으로 만든 음식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rice scorched on the bottom, or the dish made from it.

explain_en: Food sticks to the bottom of a pot or pan and burns; everyday. It describes food sticking to a pot or pan and slightly burning from heat. '타다' suggests blackened burning, while '눌어붙다' focuses on being stuck to the bottom. You also see '눌어붙은 밥' and '눌은밥'.

t90.ax: If you don't add oil, the egg can stick and burn.

examples.ko: 온몸이 땀 범벅이 되어서 샤워부터 했어요.
examples.en: I was drenched in sweat, so I showered first.
The child's face is covered in chocolate.
I said hello with a tear-streaked face.
My clothes are caked in mud, so I have to do laundry.
I made and ate a pumpkin porridge-like dish.

examples.ko: 거짓말과 소문이 범벅된 이야기라서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's a story mixed with lies and rumors, so it's hard to believe.

explain: 여러 가지가 마구 섞이거나 뒤덮인 모습을 말해서 '땀 범벅', '눈물 범벅'처럼 다른 명사 뒤에 붙여 많이 써요. 원래는 곡식과 호박 등을 섞어 쑨 음식 이름이에요. 보통 좋지 않은 것이 잔뜩 묻은 상황에 써요.

phrases.en: After exercising, my whole body is drenched in sweat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범벅과 가장 흔히 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 범벅.

phrases.example: 영화를 보고 얼굴이 눈물 범벅이 됐어요.
phrases.en: After the movie, my face was covered in tears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물이 얼굴에 가득할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the face is full of tears.

phrases.example: 청소를 안 해서 방이 먼지 범벅이에요.
phrases.en: I didn't clean, so the room is covered in dust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지저분한 것이 잔뜩 묻거나 쌓였을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something dirty covers or piles up on a place.

explain_en: It describes being all mixed up or coated in something, and is usually placed after another noun as in 땀 범벅 or 눈물 범벅. It was originally the name of a dish mixing grains and pumpkin. It usually describes being covered in something unpleasant.

examples.en: My clothes got covered with bread crumbs.
I wiped the crumbs off the desk with a tissue.
The pigeons are pecking at nothing but crumbs.

examples.ko: 부스러기 하나도 남기지 않고 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate everything without leaving a single crumb.
When you cut wood, small scraps fly around.

examples.ko: 과자 봉지 바닥에 부스러기밖에 안 남았어요.
examples.en: Only crumbs were left at the bottom of the snack bag.

explain: 과자나 빵이 부서져서 떨어진 작은 조각을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요. '나무 부스러기', '종이 부스러기'처럼 다른 재료에도 써요. '찌꺼기'는 쓰고 남은 더러운 것에 가까워서 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: The child dropped cookie crumbs on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과자가 부서져서 떨어진 작은 조각이에요. 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Small pieces broken off a snack; the most common pairing.

phrases.en: There are many paper scraps on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵이나 과자뿐 아니라 다른 재료에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not only for bread or snacks; it works with other materials too.

phrases.en: I brushed the crumbs off my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있는 작은 조각을 떨어뜨릴 때 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for brushing off small pieces that are stuck on.

explain_en: It is used most often for the small pieces that fall from broken snacks or bread. It is also used in '나무 부스러기' (wood scraps) and '종이 부스러기' (paper scraps). The similar '찌꺼기' is closer to dirty leftovers after use, so the feeling is different.

examples.en: My bag kept getting in the way, so I put it on the floor.
My long hair gets in the way.
Please clear away anything that is in the way.

examples.ko: 좁은 부엌에서 서로 거치적거리지 않게 조심해요.
examples.en: In the narrow kitchen, we are careful not to get in each other's way.
The pants were long and got in my way when I walked.
I moved the bags to one side in case they got in the way.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 걸려서 움직임이 불편하거나 일에 방해가 될 때 써요. 비슷한 '방해되다'보다 몸에 걸리는 느낌이 강해요. 사람에게 쓰면 '걸리적거리다'와 마찬가지로 '귀찮게 방해한다'는 거친 느낌이 돼요.

phrases.en: The long pants get in the way, so it's hard to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거치적거리다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '걸리적거리다'를 더 많이 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '거치적거리다', and often used even more in speech.

phrases.en: Leave the bulky stuff in the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 걸리적대는 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing an item that gets in the way.
phrases.en_equiv: luggage that gets in the way

phrases.en: I moved the chair so it wouldn't be in the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방해되지 않도록 한다는 뜻으로, 물건을 치우거나 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means 'so as not to be in the way'; used when tidying or moving things.
phrases.en_equiv: so it won't get in the way

explain_en: Use it when something catches on your body or hinders movement or work. It feels more physical, like snagging, than the similar '방해되다'. About a person it sounds harsh, as if they are annoyingly in the way.

en: to fight; to grapple; to scuffle

examples.en: In the movie, two men fight hand to hand in the street.

examples.ko: 어제 본 영화에서 두 사람이 오랫동안 격투했어요.
examples.en: In the movie I saw yesterday, two people fought for a long time.
In the movie, the hero will fight the villain.
I took a picture of them fighting.

examples.ko: 서로 붙잡고 격투하다가 둘 다 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: They grabbed each other, struggled, and both fell down.
Only after fighting for a good while did the two make up.

explain: '격투하다'는 맨몸으로 서로 치고받으며 싸울 때 써요. 말다툼은 '싸우다'나 '다투다'라고 하고, 운동 경기는 '시합하다'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '몸싸움하다'를 더 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: Fans scuffled at the soccer stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '격투하다'보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily speech than 격투하다.

phrases.en: A fight broke out in the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움이 갑자기 시작됐다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a fight suddenly breaks out.

phrases.en: That movie has many fight scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 게임에서 치고받는 장면을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to hand-to-hand fighting scenes in movies or games.

explain_en: Physical scuffle, written style. 격투하다 is for fighting with bare hands, trading blows. A verbal quarrel is 싸우다 or 다투다, and a sports match is 시합하다. In daily talk 몸싸움하다 is heard more often.

gh: general fight or argue; everyday word
struggle for a cause or rights
face off in a match; formal

p.n: The original stresses physical grappling; the replacement could include arguing.

t90.ax: I took a picture of them fighting.

en: to miss; to be sidelined; to sit out

examples.en: The captain will sit out the next game due to injury.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 두 달 동안 결장했어요.
examples.en: That player was out for two months.

examples.ko: 에이스가 결장할 때 팀 성적이 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The team's results dropped when the ace was out.
Many players are missing games because of colds.
He came back to the stadium for the first time after being out.

examples.ko: 그가 결장한 경기에서 우리 팀이 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team won the game he missed.

explain: 스포츠 뉴스에서 선수가 부상이나 징계로 경기에 나오지 못할 때 써요. 반대말은 '출전하다'예요. 학교나 모임에 안 나오는 건 '결석하다', '불참하다'라고 하고 '결장하다'는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: That player is out because of an injury.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에 못 나오는 이유를 '~으로'로 붙이는 가장 흔한 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern, giving the reason for missing a game with '~으로'.

phrases.example: 감독님 말로는 주장이 이번 경기에 결장할 것 같아요.
phrases.en: According to the coach, the captain will probably miss this game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 못 나올 것 같다고 추측할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to guess that someone won't play in an upcoming game.

phrases.en: He got hurt, so he can't play in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결장하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way to say the same thing as '결장하다'.

explain_en: Sports; a player misses a match due to injury. In sports news it is for a player who cannot play because of injury or suspension. The opposite is '출전하다'. Not showing up at school or a meeting is '결석하다' or '불참하다'; '결장하다' is not used for that.

t90.ax: Our team won the game he missed.

en: to yell; to bawl; to bellow

examples.ko: 옆집 아저씨가 밤새 고함쳐서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The man next door yelled all night, so I couldn't sleep.
The child was startled and suddenly shouted.
Don't yell like that, speak calmly.

examples.ko: 경기장에서 사람들이 목이 터져라 고함치고 있어요.
examples.en: People in the stadium are shouting at the top of their lungs.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 부모님께 고함치면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you're angry, you shouldn't yell at your parents.

examples.ko: 누가 고함치는 소리가 들려서 밖으로 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard someone shouting, so I went outside to check.

explain: '소리를 지르다'가 더 일상적인 말이고, '고함치다'는 화가 나거나 급해서 크게 외친다는 느낌이 강해요. 놀라거나 아파서 지르는 소리는 '비명'이라고 해서 구별해요.

phrases.example: 화가 나서 저도 모르게 고함을 쳤어요.
phrases.en: I was angry and yelled before I knew it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고함치다'와 뜻이 같고, '을'을 넣어 두 단어로 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as '고함치다', written as two words with '을'.

phrases.en: My friends screamed while riding the ride.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일상적인 말이고, 신나거나 놀랐을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is more everyday and can be used when excited or startled too.

phrases.en: Please don't yell, because it scares the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마세요'는 정중하게 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-지 마세요' is a polite way to tell someone not to do something.

explain_en: Stronger; shouting at the top of your voice, even cheering. '소리를 지르다' is the more everyday expression, while '고함치다' strongly suggests shouting out of anger or urgency. A cry from fright or pain is a '비명' (scream), which is a separate word.

t90.ax: Don't yell like that, speak calmly.

examples.en: People let out wild screams while riding the amusement ride.

examples.ko: 밤에 이상한 괴성이 들려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I heard a strange shriek at night and couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 괴성을 내며 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: The child is angry and running around shrieking.

examples.ko: 공연장에서 팬들이 괴성에 가까운 환호를 보냈어요.
examples.en: At the concert, fans cheered in near-shrieks.
There were weird screams from the next room, so I called the management office.

examples.ko: 영화 속 괴물이 괴성을 지르며 나타났어요.
examples.en: The monster in the movie appeared letting out a roar.

explain: '괴성을 지르다', '괴성을 내다'처럼 말해요. '비명'이 놀라거나 아파서 나오는 소리라면, '괴성'은 평범하지 않게 크고 날카로운 소리이고 신나거나 화날 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I heard a wild scream from next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이상하게 큰 소리가 들려올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an oddly loud cry is heard.

phrases.en: The child let out a wild shriek at the toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신나거나 흥분해서 크게 소리 지르는 장면에도 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also fits scenes of yelling in excitement.

phrases.en: My friend screamed in the haunted house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 아파서 나오는 소리로, '괴성'보다 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A scream from fright or pain; more common than 'goeseong'.

explain_en: It is used as '괴성을 지르다' or '괴성을 내다'. While '비명' is a scream from fear or pain, '괴성' is an unusually loud, sharp sound that can come from excitement or anger too.

t90.ax: At the concert, fans cheered in near-shrieks.

examples.en: My younger sibling keeps grumbling that they don't want to do homework.
What are you grumbling about all by yourself?
He went out, muttering complaints, and closed the door.

examples.ko: 구시렁거리지 말고 할 말이 있으면 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't mutter; if you have something to say, say it out loud.
I can hear my grandmother grumbling to herself.
It was Monday morning, so everyone grumbled their way to work.

explain: 못마땅해서 작은 소리로 혼잣말처럼 불평하는 모습이에요. '불평하다'는 분명하게 말하는 느낌이지만, 이 말은 알아듣기 어렵게 중얼거리는 느낌이 있어요. '구시렁대다'로도 말해요.

phrases.en: Dad cleans while grumbling to himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 말하지 않고 혼자 불평하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For someone grumbling quietly to themselves.

phrases.en: Why do you keep grumbling?
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and heard more often in speech.

phrases.example: 불만이 있으면 구시렁거리지 말고 말해 주세요.
phrases.en: If you're unhappy, don't mutter. Just tell me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작게 불평하지 말고 분명히 말하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request to stop muttering and say it clearly instead.

explain_en: To mutter in a low voice, annoyed, often about trivial things. It describes muttering complaints under your breath, as if talking to yourself. '불평하다' sounds like complaining clearly, while this one has a feel of mumbling so that it's hard to make out. It can also be said as '구시렁대다'.

t90.ax: What are you grumbling about all by yourself?

examples.en: The enemy launched a surprise attack on the village at dawn.

examples.ko: 경찰이 밤에 창고를 기습해서 범인을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The police raided the warehouse at night and caught the culprit.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 우리 진영을 기습하는 바람에 졌어요.
examples.en: We lost because the other team hit our side by surprise.

examples.ko: 그들이 기습할 거라고는 아무도 생각하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Nobody expected that they would attack by surprise.
The cat pounced on the toy as if ambushing it.

examples.ko: 군대는 비 오는 날을 노려 기습하고 도망갔어요.
examples.en: The army chose a rainy day, struck by surprise and fled.

explain: '공격하다'는 그냥 치는 것이고, '기습하다'는 상대가 준비하지 못한 때를 노려요. 주로 뉴스나 이야기에서 '~을/를 기습하다' 형태로 써요.

phrases.en: The enemy made a surprise attack at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기습하다'를 명사로 쓴 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase built on the idea of '기습하다'.

phrases.en: The village was ambushed at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당하는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one who is attacked.

phrases.en: A robber attacked the shop late at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기습하다'와 비슷하지만 갑자기 덮쳐서 해친다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to '기습하다' but stresses suddenly pouncing and causing harm.

explain_en: '공격하다' just means to attack, while '기습하다' means to strike when the other side is not ready. It mostly appears in news and stories, in the pattern '~을/를 기습하다'.

examples.en: An angry customer made a scene in the shop.

examples.ko: 제발 오늘 회의에서 깽판 놓지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't wreck the meeting today.

examples.ko: 네가 깽판 쳐서 계획이 다 엉망이 됐어요.
examples.en: You messed it up, and now the whole plan is a wreck.

examples.ko: 일부러 깽판 놓으려고 온 사람 같아요.
examples.en: He seems like someone who came on purpose to cause trouble.

examples.ko: 동생이 방에서 깽판을 친 걸 엄마가 보셨어요.
examples.en: Mom saw that my little brother had trashed the room.
A ruckus broke out at the party and everyone was shocked.

explain: '깽판을 치다', '깽판을 놓다'처럼 거의 이 형태로 써요. 일이 잘 안 되게 망치거나 소란을 피울 때 쓰는 구어체라서 친구나 가족 사이에서 자연스럽고, 격식 있는 자리에서는 '망치다'나 '소란을 피우다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 술에 취한 사람이 식당에서 깽판을 쳤어요.
phrases.en: A drunk person caused a scene in the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소란을 피우며 난장판을 만들 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for making a ruckus and causing chaos.

phrases.example: 누가 모임에서 깽판을 놓았는지 아직도 몰라요.
phrases.en: I still don't know who ruined the gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깽판을 치다'와 비슷해요. 일을 망치게 방해한다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '깽판을 치다', with a feel of wrecking or sabotaging an event.

phrases.en: You shouldn't make a disturbance in public places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격식 있는 자리에서 쓸 수 있는 말이에요. '깽판'은 구어체라서 이 표현이 더 정중해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase suitable for formal settings. '깽판' is colloquial, so this is more polite.

explain_en: It is used almost only in the forms '깽판을 치다' and '깽판을 놓다'. It is colloquial for ruining something or causing a ruckus, so it fits among friends and family. In formal settings people say '망치다' or '소란을 피우다'.

en: to grunt; to groan with effort; to whimper

examples.en: The puppy is whining in front of the door.
I grunted and struggled carrying the heavy box by myself.
The homework is hard, so I've been struggling with it for an hour.
Stop straining by yourself and let's lift it together.
The baby puppy whimpers as it looks for its mother.
I huffed and puffed up the stairs carrying the luggage.

explain: 강아지가 내는 낑낑 소리에도 쓰고, 사람이 힘들게 애쓰는 모습에도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 '끙끙대다'보다 힘을 쓰느라 소리를 내는 느낌이 강해요. '낑낑거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: The puppy is whimpering, maybe because it's hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낑낑대다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with the headword.

phrases.en: The man lifted the luggage, grunting with effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 애쓰면서 다른 동작을 할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for doing something while straining.

phrases.example: 문 밖에서 강아지가 낑낑 소리를 내요.
phrases.en: A puppy is whining outside the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리 자체를 강조할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that emphasizes the sound itself.

explain_en: It can describe the whimpering sound a puppy makes, and also a person struggling hard at something. Used for people, it suggests straining and making noise from effort, more so than '끙끙대다'. '낑낑거리다' means the same.

t90.ax: The puppy is whining in front of the door.

examples.ko: 동생이 설거지 시간만 되면 슬쩍 내빼요.
examples.en: My younger sibling slips away whenever it's time to wash dishes.

examples.ko: 친구가 계산할 때가 되자 어느새 내뺐어요.
examples.en: When it came time to pay, my friend had already slipped away.

examples.ko: 사고를 내고 그냥 내빼면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cause an accident and just run off.

examples.ko: 고양이가 사람을 보자마자 담 너머로 내빼는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a cat dash over the wall as soon as it saw a person.

examples.ko: 일이 힘들다고 혼자 내빼지 말고 같이 해요.
examples.en: Don't bail out on your own just because the work is hard; let's do it together.

examples.ko: 몰래 내빼려고 했는데 선생님한테 딱 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I tried to sneak away, but the teacher caught me.

explain: '도망가다'보다 훨씬 구어적이고, 곤란한 일이나 책임에서 슬쩍 빠져나갈 때 자주 써요. 친구나 가족 사이의 편한 말투에 어울려서 격식 있는 글에는 잘 안 써요. 진짜 무서워서 달아나는 상황이면 '도망가다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 청소 시간이 되자 친구가 슬쩍 내뺐어요.
phrases.en: When cleaning time came, my friend slipped away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '슬쩍'이 붙어서 눈치채지 못하게 빠져나가는 모습이 더 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '슬쩍', the sneaky way of slipping out becomes clearer.

phrases.en: When things got serious, he ran off by himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 두고 혼자 빠져나갈 때 써요. 가족이나 친구 사이에서 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone slips away alone and leaves others behind. A casual word among family and friends.

phrases.example: 중요한 순간에 내빼지 말고 같이 해요.
phrases.en: Don't run off at the important moment, let's do it together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형이에요. 책임을 피하지 말라고 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to ask someone lightly not to dodge responsibility.

explain_en: It is much more colloquial than '도망가다' and is often used when someone slips out of a tough job or responsibility. It suits casual talk among friends or family and is rarely used in formal writing. For truly fleeing in fear, '도망가다' sounds more natural.
